services.name: Tree Root Intrusions
services.lead: Roots work into a lateral at the joints, then thicken until the line stops. We cut them out of the pipe with a jet and film what is left, so you know whether the line needs repair.
blocks: Where the roots get in

Roots are drawn to the moisture in a sewer lateral. A loose joint or a small crack is enough of an opening, and over several seasons the growth fills the pipe. Medina's older streets near the square have mature trees and older lateral pipe, so this is a common find on camera.
Clearing the roots does not close the opening. If the camera shows a gap, plan on repair or a regular cleaning schedule.
What the jet does
A root-cutting nozzle runs the length of the line and clears the mass back to the pipe wall at a pressure the pipe can take. Debris flushes down the line with the water.
The second camera pass shows the result. If the wall is cracked or offset, you get that footage to keep.
County and homeowner lines

Medina County Sanitary Engineers maintain the sewer main and the lateral inside the public right-of-way. The lateral from your house to the main is yours. The county advises that lateral repair or replacement needs a permit from its Permits Division before work begins, so keep footage of any damaged section.
faqs: Will roots grow back after jetting?
They can. Jetting removes the roots in the pipe, not the opening they used. The camera shows whether the pipe needs repair.
Does a root problem mean my sewer line is broken?
Roots can enter through a gap or a loose joint. Their presence does not show how much damage there is. Camera footage does.
Do I need a permit to repair a lateral?
The county advises a permit from its Permits Division before repair or replacement. Ask the county before any digging.

services.name: Severe Grease and Sludge
services.lead: Grease sets on the pipe wall and keeps collecting soap, food and sediment. A jet strips it back to the wall, and the camera confirms what came out.
blocks: Why grease is hard to clear

Fats leave a kitchen as a liquid, cool in the line and harden. Each wash adds another film, and the opening gets smaller until a drain slows or stops. A cable can open a channel and leave most of the buildup behind.
Hot water does not fix it. It moves the grease farther down the line, where it cools again.
Shops and kitchens around the square
The rebuilt downtown blocks around Medina's square hold restaurants and shops that put grease through their lines every day. Jetting on a schedule keeps those lines open between backups.
Grease line jetting is different from servicing a grease trap or interceptor. Know which one you have before booking.
After the clean
Keep fats out of the drain and wipe pans before washing. A line that was cleaned to the wall stays clear longer when the buildup is not replaced.
Ask for the post-jet footage. It shows the wall, not just the flow.
faqs: Is hot water enough to clear grease?
Usually not. It can push the grease deeper into the line before it sets again.
Is jetting the same as cleaning a grease trap?
No. A trap or interceptor is separate equipment. Jetting cleans the drain line.
Can a home line have severe grease buildup?
Yes. Kitchen lines in homes collect grease and soap over time, especially with heavy cooking.

services.name: Mineral and Scale Deposits
services.lead: Scale is a hard, rough layer that forms inside older pipe. It narrows the line a little at a time and catches whatever else passes through.
blocks: How scale narrows a line

Minerals in water settle on the pipe wall, and iron pipe can rust. The surface roughens, and a rough surface traps paper and grease sooner than a smooth one. The pipe loses diameter without any single clog to blame.
That is why a line that is slow for months can suddenly stop.
Older streets, newer subdivisions

Homes from Medina's canal-era and early town blocks may be on older lateral pipe, while later subdivisions have newer lines. Age alone does not decide the material or condition, because sections get repaired and replaced over time.
The camera shows what the wall looks like today.
Jetting a scaled pipe
A suitable nozzle can break scale loose and wash it out of a sound line. If the pipe is thin or corroded, the camera tells us before we start, and we may recommend a different approach.
You get the before and after footage either way.
faqs: Can scale be removed?
Often it can be reduced in a sound pipe with the right nozzle. A weak pipe may need a different plan.
Does scale mean the pipe has to be replaced?
Not necessarily. Inspection shows how much wall is left.
How do I know if I have scale?
A slow line with no clear blockage is a clue. Only the camera can confirm it.

services.name: Recurring Clogs and Slow Drains
services.lead: If the same drain clogs again in a few weeks, the first fix did not touch the cause. We look at the pattern, film the line and clean the wall.
blocks: Start with what it is doing
Note which fixtures are slow, how long the relief lasts and whether it changes with laundry or rain. One slow sink points to a branch. A basement drain or several fixtures together point to the main.
Tell us that on the form. It helps us decide where to set up the hose.
Why the clog returns
A cable opens a path through the blockage and leaves the coating on the wall. The path fills again. A sag, an offset joint or a root entry can also hold debris in place.
Jetting cleans the wall and the camera shows if something else is wrong.
Public or private line

If your neighbors back up at the same time, call Medina County Sanitary Engineers as well. They maintain the main and the part of the lateral in the right-of-way. The part from your house to the main is yours, and footage helps show where the trouble is.
faqs: Why does my drain keep clogging?
The buildup on the pipe wall may be untouched, or something in the line holds debris. A camera shows which.
Is a slow drain urgent?
It can turn into a backup quickly if several fixtures are affected.
Can I tell if the problem is on the county side?
Camera footage can help. If it shows a clear line to the main, the trouble is likely elsewhere. Confirm with the county.

services.name: Preventative Maintenance
services.lead: A recorded baseline and a cleaning schedule that fits how the line is used. It is easier to plan than an emergency.
blocks: Begin with a baseline
One camera pass records the material, joints and buildup. Later visits compare against it. Keep the footage with your property records and note where the cleanout is.
It also gives you something to show if a repair question comes up.
Set the interval by use
A restaurant kitchen line needs a shorter interval than a spare bathroom. A line with a history of roots needs more checking than one with a clean record.
There is no single schedule for every property, so we base it on the footage and your backup history.
What maintenance cannot do
Cleaning keeps a sound line sound. It does not repair a break, replace a section or service a septic system. If the footage shows damage, we say so and you decide what comes next.
faqs: How often should I schedule jetting?
It depends on use, pipe condition and past backups. A baseline camera pass helps set it.
Is maintenance needed if there are no backups?
Properties with grease, roots or repeat clogs benefit most.
Does maintenance replace repair?
No. It keeps a sound line clear and shows when repair is needed.

guides.name: How Hydro Jetting Works
guides.lead: A pump, a hose and a nozzle, plus a camera at the start and the end. Here is the visit from the first look to the final pass.
blocks: The equipment
A jetting unit pushes water through a hose to a nozzle. Some ports face forward to break up a blockage. Others face back and pull the hose along while the jets scour the wall.
We pick the nozzle and pressure to suit the pipe, because an older line and a modern one do not take the same treatment.
The camera passes
Before jetting, a camera shows the blockage, the pipe material and any damage. After, a second pass shows the wall. The footage is how you check the result for yourself.
Access is through a cleanout or an open drain. If there is no cleanout, we plan the access point first.
What jetting cannot do
Cleaning does not repair a break, a sag or an offset joint. If the camera finds one, you see the footage and decide on the next step.
faqs: Is jetting safe for all pipes?
No. The pipe condition decides, which is why we run the camera first.
Do I need a cleanout?
It makes access simpler. Without one, we plan another opening.
How long does a visit take?
It depends on the line and access. Describe the problem on the form for a better idea.

guides.name: Hydro Jetting vs Snaking
guides.lead: A cable opens a hole. A jet cleans the pipe. Which one you need depends on what is in the line and how it has been behaving.
blocks: What a snake does well
A cable bores through a stoppage and often restores flow quickly. For a one-time clog in a single fixture, that can be enough.
It tends to leave the coating on the wall, so the same line may clog again soon.
What a jet does well
Water scours the full inside of the pipe and flushes debris away. It suits grease, scale, sludge and roots in a sound line.
It is not right for every pipe. Weak or failing lines may need another approach after the camera pass.
How to choose
Repeat clogs, several fixtures slowing together, or a kitchen with heavy grease use point toward jetting. A one-off stoppage may only need a cable.
Tell us the pattern on the form and we will say which fits.
faqs: Is jetting always better?
No. A simple stoppage may only need a cable. Jetting is stronger against buildup on the wall.
Can a jet damage a pipe?
It can damage a weak or failing pipe, which is why the camera comes first.
Which should I ask for?
Describe the symptoms and we will recommend one.
